docs.title: Cloudmesh AI Theme Guide
docs.text:
Welcome to the official guide for the Cloudmesh AI Theme.

This package provides a centralized branding system for the entire Cloudmesh AI ecosystem. Instead of duplicating CSS, logos, and favicons across dozens of project repositories, this theme package allows you to apply a standardized look and feel via a simple configuration change.

docs.title: What this theme provides
docs.text:
• Unified Branding: Automatically injects the "Cloudmesh AI" site name and a standardized layout.
  • Custom Styling: Applies a curated set of CSS overrides to align with the Cloudmesh AI brand.
  • Shared Assets: Provides high-quality logos and SVG favicons that are automatically available to your site.
  • Material Base: Leverages the power and accessibility of the Material for MkDocs theme.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: To get started, head over to the Installation Guide to learn how to add this theme to your project.

docs.title: Development and Contribution
docs.text: This guide explains how to modify the theme and contribute improvements.

docs.title: Local Development
docs.text:
To make changes to the theme and see them reflected in your projects immediately, install the package in editable mode:

cd cloudmesh-ai-theme
make install

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text:
The theme includes a verification suite to ensure that the package builds and renders correctly.

make test

docs.title: Previewing Changes
docs.text:
You can preview the theme's own documentation to see how changes affect the layout:

make view

docs.title: Contribution Workflow
docs.text:
1. Create a new branch for your feature or fix.
  2. Implement your changes in src/cloudmesh_ai_theme/.
  3. Verify your changes using make test.
  4. Commit your changes and open a Pull Request.

docs.title: Installation and Usage
docs.text: The cloudmesh-ai-theme is distributed as a Python package, making it easy to manage as a dependency for your documentation site.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install the theme using pip:

pip install cloudmesh-ai-theme

If you are using a requirements.txt or pyproject.toml file, add cloudmesh-ai-theme to your dependencies.

docs.title: Primary Method (Recommended)
docs.text:
The simplest way to use the theme is to specify it by name in your mkdocs.yml file. This method automatically applies all branding, styles, and assets.

theme:
  name: cloudmesh-ai-theme

docs.title: Configuration Options
docs.text: You can customize the theme while maintaining the Cloudmesh AI layout. Currently, the following options are supported:

docs.title: Primary Color
docs.text:
Change the primary accent color of the theme:

theme:
  name: cloudmesh-ai-theme
  primary_color: "#ff0000" # Example: Red

docs.title: Logo and Favicon
docs.text:
You can override the default Cloudmesh AI logo and favicon by specifying their paths in your mkdocs.yml. SVG favicons are recommended for better scalability.

theme:
  name: cloudmesh-ai-theme
  logo: assets/my-logo.png
  favicon: assets/my-favicon.svg

docs.title: Alternative: Manual Asset Deployment
docs.text:
If you need direct access to the CSS and image files within your project directory (e.g., for further local overrides), you can deploy the assets manually.

  1. Deploy assets: Use a deployment script or copy files from the package installation directory into docs/theme/.
  2. Reference assets in mkdocs.yml: ```yaml extra_css:
    • theme/custom.css

theme: favicon: theme/assets/favicon.svg logo: theme/assets/logo-white.png name: material ```

docs.title: Maintainer's Guide
docs.text: This section is for developers responsible for the long-term maintenance of the theme.

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
cloudmesh-ai-theme/
├── .github/workflows/  # CI/CD pipelines
├── src/
│   └── cloudmesh_ai_theme/
│       ├── __init__.py  # Package logic & versioning
│       ├── assets/      # Logos and favicons
│       ├── css/         # Custom stylesheets
│       └── theme/       # MkDocs templates (main.html)
├── docs/               # Documentation source
├── tests/              # Verification suite
├── VERSION             # Single source of truth for version
├── pyproject.toml      # Build system & metadata
├── Makefile            # Project automation
└── README.md           # GitHub landing page

docs.title: Version Management
docs.text: The version is managed in the VERSION file at the root of the repository. To bump the version: 1. Edit the VERSION file (e.g., change 7.0.5 to 7.0.6). 2. Commit the change: bash git add VERSION git commit -m "Bump version to 7.0.6"

docs.title: Release Process
docs.text: Releases are automated via GitHub Actions. To trigger a new release: 1. Create a git tag following the v* pattern: bash git tag v7.0.6 git push origin v7.0.6 2. The GitHub Action will automatically build the distributions and upload them.

docs.title: Publishing to PyPI
docs.text: The theme is published to PyPI to allow easy installation via pip. This is typically handled by the release workflow or can be done manually using twine.
